also: wait here till I come back

terms.grammar: imperative of opperior, opperīrī, oppertus sum, with hīc
evidence: Ter. And. 714: parumper mē opperīre hīc
terms.comment: The comedians’ everyday word for waiting for someone who will be back in a moment, usually with hīc and often parumper. To tell a child simply to stay put, Hīc manē.

evidence: Ter. Eun. 534–535: at tū apud nōs hīc manē, dum redeat ipsa
Plaut. Asin. 597: quīn tū hīc manēs?

phrases.latin: Hīc mē opperīre, dum pānem emō.
phrases.english: Wait for me here while I buy the bread.

phrases.latin: dum exeō, parumper mē opperīre hīc. — Quāpropter? — Ita factōst opus.
phrases.english: Wait for me here a moment till I come out. — What for? — It has to be done.

phrases.latin: tū hīc opperīre, jam ego faxō exībit senex
phrases.english: you wait here; I’ll have the old man out in a moment

phrases.latin: at tū apud nōs hīc manē, dum redeat ipsa
phrases.english: but you stay here with us till she comes back herself

sources: Lewis & Short: opperior · Lewis & Short: maneo
